Achieving Mission 300 requires a fundamental shift in how we approach Energy Access!⚡️ 

Yesterday, in a timely and critical session organized by The World Bank and ESMAP - Energy Sector Management Assistance Program - Energy Sector Management Assistance Program at the #SEforALLForum in Barbados, we discussed what it will take to scale distributed renewable energy and unlock financing to reach 300 million people by 2030: 

1️⃣ Distributed renewables must be embedded in national energy strategies: Clear interconnection policies are critical to ensuring mini-grids can complement, rather than compete with, national grids. When integrated effectively, they could provide up to 11% of new electricity connections. 

2️⃣ The cost of capital is a barrier to scaling clean energy: High borrowing costs and debt burdens are locking out investment. Policy and financial de-risking mechanisms, including debt-for-energyswaps and financial instruments, must be expanded. 

3️⃣ A whole-of-society approach is essential: Civil society, local leadership, and communities must be at the center of designing and scaling energy solutions, as seen in Guinea’s successful decentralized projects. 

Technology alone will not deliver M300. Policy and regulatory reforms, coupled with strategic financing, are needed to turn solutions into large-scale impact.🌐

UNDP and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) are connecting policy, finance, and innovation to drive transformation. We are moving beyond business-as-usual approaches and rethinking financing clean energy to drive meaningful and lasting development impact. 

Through initiatives like the Africa Minigrids Program, Solar for Health, and financial de-risking instruments, we are committed to scale clean energy through collaboration!🤝⚡️
